source:
Create a Roblox exploration and co-op game called "The Forgotten Fairground," a massive abandoned amusement park that shut down suddenly years ago for an unknown reason and was never reopened. The overall mood is mysterious and eerie with a light horror touch, featuring nighttime lighting and old colored lights, some still flickering and others dead. Rides are frozen mid-motion, carts hang stuck on the tracks, vines and overgrowth cover the fences, and old tickets litter the ground.
The world should include multiple unique locations:
A giant, stopped Ferris wheel players can climb to reach the highest point on the map.
A hall of mirrors filled with visual puzzles and hidden passages.
A broken roller coaster that players must repair piece by piece to get it running again.
An abandoned circus tent with an old stage and scattered clown costumes.
A prize games area with locked-up booths hiding rare treasures and rewards.
A dark underground horror tunnel with strange sounds and unknown creatures.
A secret control room in the watchtower containing clues explaining why the park was suddenly shut down.
An old food cart (ice cream and popcorn) that can be turned into a player hangout spot or shop.

image_prompt.text: A giant stopped Ferris wheel, visible from everywhere in the park and climbable to the highest point on the map
Hidden passages tucked behind the mirrors and around the park's dead ends, rewarding players who poke around
Winding midway paths through the fairground linking the rides, littered with old tickets and cracked underfoot
Locked-up prize booths that stay shut until players have earned or found the way in
A hall of mirrors: a maze of reflective walls with visual puzzles and concealed passages
A broken roller coaster, track and cars scattered in pieces, that players repair section by section to get running again
An abandoned circus tent with an old performance stage and clown costumes strewn about
A prize games area of shuttered booths
A dark underground horror tunnel running beneath the park
A secret control room at the top of the watchtower, papered with clues about the sudden shutdown
An old ice cream and popcorn food cart that can serve as a player hangout or shop
Rides frozen mid-motion with carts hanging stuck on their tracks
Old coloured bulbs strung across the park, some flickering, some dead

layout_placement.text: Rare treasures and rewards hidden inside the locked prize booths, and clues in the control room

notes: Pipeline was raised beyond the picked options: the underground tunnel stacks a surface beneath the park (P2) and the tent, control room and tunnel are entered from outside (P3). No Adventure option carries either tag, so the cost comes from free-text requests rather than from a pick.
Adventure has no enterable-building option at all, so four interior locations had to be written as free text.
Nine named locations in one contiguous open world is a lot for a single top-down frame at district scale; decomposition may be needed.

open_questions.ask: What is the co-op objective - restore the park, uncover why it closed, or is it free exploration?
'Massive' - should the park read as a few hundred studs across or a full region?
Are all nine locations on one continuous surface, or should the tunnel and interiors be separate maps?

theme: Abandoned carnival, eerie with a light horror touch - night, overgrown, rusted and decayed. Horror and Post-Apocalyptic both fit; leaning Horror.

coverage_missing.ask: Is there a win condition - reopening the park, solving the shutdown - or is this open-ended exploration?
How many players co-operate at once, and does that change the size of the hub areas?
Should the roller coaster repair gate access to other areas, or is it a standalone activity?

answers.ask: What is the co-op objective - restore the park, uncover why it closed, or is it free exploration?
answers.answer: The co-op objective is to explore the fairground, repair the broken roller coaster together, and uncover clues in the watchtower control room explaining why the park shut down.

answers.ask: 'Massive' - should the park read as a few hundred studs across or a full region?
answers.answer: Make it a few hundred studs across: dense enough to feel like a massive abandoned park, but compact and easy to explore as a single playable map.

answers.ask: Are all nine locations on one continuous surface, or should the tunnel and interiors be separate maps?
answers.answer: Keep all locations on one continuous park map; interiors such as the hall of mirrors, circus tent, booths, control room, and underground tunnel are entered directly from that surface.
